title: Advancing utilization and control of individual auricular muscles: Development of a training protocol for voluntary and side-specific control of each extrinsic ear muscle
summary:
Humans have three muscles on each ear, which attach to the front, top and back of the ear (called extrinsic ear muscles/extrinsic auricular muscles). These extrinsic ear muscles have no physiological function in everyday life and are therefore to be regarded as evolutionary remnants. Due to this fact, they offer the unique opportunity to use them for the voluntary control of various medical and lifestyle devices. For example, it would be possible for a patient with facial nerve paralysis to operate a pacemaker with which individual facial muscles could be contracted. Similarly, a patient with paraplegia could control an electric wheelchair using their extrinsic ear muscles. Healthy people could also benefit from controlling various devices using their ear muscles - for example, by operating Bluetooth headphones using this option.
However, these applications are only possible if each of the six extrinsic ear muscles can be made to contract individually at will.
Building on the results of previous studies, the aim of this study is therefore to develop a reliable training protocol for the extrinsic ear muscles that will enable patients with facial nerve palsy to voluntarily control all six extrinsic ear muscles individually.
To this end, the training paradigm will first be trialled on healthy volunteers and further improved before being tested on the target group - patients with facial nerve palsy.

interventions.name:
20 healthy subject
20 patients with peripheral facial palsy
Intervention: 10-day biofeedback training with OEMG measurements, 2 fMRI measurements (pre- and post-training)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patients:
- Patients from the Facial Nerve Centre at Jena University Hospital with peripheral facial nerve palsy
- Patients who cannot move their ears voluntarily

2. Healthy subjects:
- No history of facial nerve palsy
- No previous neurological or psychiatric illnesses
- Subjects who cannot move their ears voluntarily
Exclusion criteria:
1. Patients:
- diagnosed neurological diseases (in addition to peripheral facial nerve palsy) that have the potential to negatively influence the measurements
- Medication that can negatively influence the measurements
- Patients who can move their ears voluntarily
- Contraindications to MRI measurements (e.g. pacemaker, metal in the body, claustrophobia)
- Previous surgery on the auricles or middle ear surgery
- Lack of consent
- Pregnancy at the time of measurement

2. Healthy subjects:
- Diagnosed neurological diseases that have the potential to negatively influence the measurements
- Medication that can negatively influence the measurements
- Subjects who can move their ears voluntarily
- Contraindications to MRI measurements (e.g. pacemaker, metal in the body, claustrophobia)
- Previous surgery on the auricles or middle ear surgery
- Lack of consent
- Pregnancy at the time of the measurement
